Where Climate Week
Comes to Dream

An urban refuge to cohere our dreams into a resilient, regenerative future.
September 21–27 · East Village, New York.

We are inviting the builders, dreamers, and doers who are grappling with the Metacrisis and building a prosocial, regenerative future. We’ve partnered up with New York City’s oldest organic vegan restaurant to create a space for cross-pollination and convergence between worlds as we consider how to future-proof ourselves, our communities, and our planet.

Come nourish your mind, body, and spirit.

This space exists to support you.

The refuge

East Sixth Street, five minutes from Tompkins Square Park.

Caravan of Dreams has fed the East Village since 1991.

Its name echoes a Sufi teaching. The mystic Bahaudin Naqshband described humanity as a dream-caravan: individuals traveling together, yet each suspended in their own subjective reality, carried by their own hopes and illusions.

This week, we hope to gather those dreams together, right here in NYC.

As you enter the space, you’ll discover a bohemian restaurant with a small stage and a kitchen that runs all day: warm coffee, healthy snacks, exquisite plates, and drinks with or without alcohol. Behind it, the private Dream Room has a screen and A/V, for the conversations that want a door closed.

The doors are open from 11 AM to 11 PM, all week, for the curious locals and the weary travelers alike.

The Dream Room

One room, multiple configurations

Tell us what you need, and we will find ways of supporting you.

Ticketedfrom $200 an hour Cover it through your own private ticket sales.
Dinnerfrom $300 an hour, spent on food A dish averages about $30, so 20 people ordering food easily covers your costs.

These rates are our raw costs; we’re not making any money. If cost is an issue, please let us know. We will try to find a way to accommodate and support you.

The perfect room for small, intimate events. It comes with screens, a/v, microphones, speakers, and a host of seating configurations.

Theatre

Approximately 40 to 45 seats

Rows facing the front. The shape for talks, screenings and panels, where everyone is pointed the same way.

Discussion

About 15 people

Sitting across from one another, with the table down the middle. The shape for working lunches and conversations that need everyone in earshot.

Fishbowl

A ring of about 20 observers

A conversation in the center, witnessed by others. Anyone can jump in and tap the other out.

This space can be configured in many different ways! If you want to host an event that follows our and would like to apply for a spot, please let us know!

The curation

Our guidelines

We want to curate the best possible mixture of humans. We hope your event fits these broad criteria:

  • It cross-pollinates. It lives at the intersection of worlds that do not usually share a room.
  • It builds capacity. People leave with actions they can take.
  • It senses into the long arc of time. Forget quarterly profits and short-term false solutions.
  • It sells nothing. No pitches, no demos: this is not a corporate demo day.
Field trip

East Village Tour: Energy and Innovation

Wednesday, September 23 · 11 AM–12:30 PM · departs and ends at Caravan of Dreams

Drop your bag at Caravan of Dreams and walk with Wendy Brawer, eco designer and mapmaker, exploring the local landscape of climate and care projects that address the crux of the metacrisis. We’ll see sites on the new LES Power Green Map-zine where the energy transition is taking root. Along the way, Wendy will introduce her open source community mapping initiative and invite you to consider making a Green Map where you live. You’ll be back at Caravan by lunch time.

Lunch afterward at Caravan of Dreams, in the public front of house.
